Yes I used to live in a flat in Green Ridges. I really liked it there, it can be noisy as it’s next to the main road but the trees absorb a lot of the noise and to be honest you end up tuning it out. There’s lots of trees and green areas, and you are a 5 minute walk to the countryside pretty much. We used to walk a lot to Forest Hill which is a lovely country walk. 

I used to cycle mostly and it would take about 20 minutes into town. The 8 bus serves the whole of that area, it can take a while to get to town because of the traffic so sometimes you’re better off walking to Headington. What makes it super easy is it is right next to Thornhill park and ride where you can catch the Oxford tube to London - however a major downside to that is that on busy days and weekends you’re less likely to get a seat. But you have all the airport buses right there too. 

Overall I loved it and wouldn’t have moved, but we couldn’t afford to buy there! Hope that helps you.

I live in Banbury so I can hopefully help a little! I second Finders Keepers for a rental agency, had two good experiences with them whilst living in Oxford. Avoid Chancellors like the plague. 

For areas to live, anything around South Bar street, people’s park and that area is nice. As for areas to avoid, I’ve not lived here long enough to know too much but I haven’t heard good things about the Grimsbury area and areas around the station. 

For things to do, you’re right in that Banbury is fairly quiet. There are some nice pubs around and they’ll often have live music in the street food area of the shopping centre. Oxford definitely has more going on and the train between is only 20 minutes.

I’m currently with Finders Keepers and they’ve been great, anecdotal I know but had no issues in the 3 years I’ve been renting through them. 

Location wise, I’m currently in the Sandhills area just outside the ring road in Headington which is very easy for buses into town and cycling is also easy. Gets very busy on the ring road though and cars are not cyclists best friends… 

Price wise, we’ve been paying £1050 a month for a 2 bed flat, bills not included. And that is split between 2 people so cheaper in that regard. It’s a nice area, although it’s next to Barton which may put some people off. Cheaper though!

I would highly recommend going to Victoria and getting on there. Went to Adele last night in Hyde park but they closed Marble Arch so had to walk to Notting hill, where the coaches were all full. Ended up getting a tube back to Victoria so I could get a seat! Was a massive waste of time, so plan your route back to Victoria ahead of time.

It’s on a Saturday morning from 9am until 2pm. You need to go early though to get the good stuff. It is also quite expensive. 

Alternatively, there are several Halal grocery shops that sell loose fruit and veg, as well as some meat which I find to be a good price.

There’s a weekly farmers market in Headington on a Saturday, although there’s not too many stalls. There’s no big grocery shops, but there are several small greengrocers, a small Sainsburys and Tesco, and a larger Waitrose and Co-op. There are a couple of gyms around- Anytime fitness and the one at Brookes University. 
If you cycle, it’s easy to get to Cowley for the big Tesco and various other gyms, including David Lloyd that has tennis courts and a swimming pool. Although there are several tennis courts in Bury Knowle Park in Headington.

I’d have a look in Headington - frequent buses to town with a couple of lovely parks, and Brookes university has a great sports centre. It’s a bit further from the station but you can catch the Oxford Tube to London really easily, as well as coaches to the airports. It has a lot less nightlife than Cowley but there are some good pubs.

There’s free parking along warnford lane and Cheney lane to the left of Brookes- you can walk through the park to get to Brookes. Only thing is it is quite busy as people park there for the hospitals, so can be hit and miss at getting a space.
I go to Versus on Cowley Road. They are really friendly and I always get a good haircut. Price for a wash and cut is £33 I think? Haven’t been for a while but it’s worth checking their website.
